synthetic_test_plan: ConnectorWorkLine.tsx is the shared 'work line' block used by two screens: the connectors screen (through ConnectorWorks.tsx, one line per import work) and the draft overview (through DraftRoot.tsx, one line for the draft's validation work). At base_commit the block hard-codes t_i18n('Status') as the label of its state field, so the approved-draft page labels the validation progress of the draft 'Status' — the wording the platform now uses for the draft workflow status, which is what the issue's screenshot shows. The fix makes the label a per-call-site decision (an optional statusLabel prop) and the draft call site supplies the validation wording. The spec renders the REAL DraftRoot (fed a draft fixture across the relay boundary) and, as the reference context, the REAL ConnectorWorks list, both of which render the REAL ConnectorWorkLine through the REAL Label/TaskStatus/Tag components. Stand-ins exist only for LEAF modules that cannot run offline (react-relay, relay-runtime, react-router-dom, rxjs, ramda, dompurify, js-base64, mdi-material-ui, @mui/icons-material, @mui/styles, i18n, Loader/ErrorNotFound/Breadcrumbs, the design-system Button/Card/CardTitle, the Drawer shell, ConnectorWorksErrorLine, parseWorkErrors, the routed draft screens, relay/environment, Security, utils/Time and the useGranted/useDraftContext/useHelper/useSwitchDraft hooks) — never ConnectorWorkLine, DraftRoot, ConnectorWorks, Label, TaskStatus, useApiMutation, utils/String or @mui/material.
anti_overfit: No assertion compares a label against a string copied out of the fix. A work line is read back from the DOM as {label, value} pairs; the state field is LOCATED BY ITS VALUE (the work state it is displaying) and the assertion is then made on that field's LABEL, so the scored contract is the observable mapping 'call site -> wording of the state field' rather than one author's literal. The set of work states is read live from the GraphQL schema's `enum State` (opencti-platform/opencti-graphql/config/schema/opencti.graphql) instead of being hard-coded, and every state is driven through both call sites, so a fix that special-cases the state visible in the screenshot cannot pass. A second, fully disjoint draft/work fixture (different ids, names, timings, counters, state, draft status) repeats the check so nothing can be tied to the reported values. The only wording constraint on the new label is that it mentions the validation it reports on (case-insensitive /validation/) and is not the generic 'Status' — capitalisation and any longer phrasing pass. The p2p side pins what must NOT change: the generic connectors work line keeps the platform's 'Status' wording for every state, every other field label of the line is byte-identical between the two contexts, the state value itself still renders in both, and the name/timings/counters of the draft validation work are unchanged. Verified against two independent correct implementations and four band-aids (see NOTES.md).
